sections.html:
Lancaster sits in southwestern Dallas County, roughly 15 minutes south of Dallas, with Interstates 20, 35 and 45 close by. The city covers 33 square miles and its housing runs from single-family streets to a sizable share of multi-family property. Dallas County handles the tax bill. Commute, school district and condition drive most buyer decisions here, so having those three answers ready saves days.

Lancaster Independent School District runs the public schools, and shoppers will want to confirm the campus assigned to each address. Add the DART light rail link toward downtown Dallas and the nearby park system, and you have the selling points most buyers mention.

sections.h2: When Dallas County taxes are due
sections.html:
Dallas County mails statements in October once local budgets and rates are set, and payment is expected on receipt. Pay after January 31 and the account is delinquent, with penalty and interest required by state law. A tax bill you never received does not erase the debt. Mailed payments count on their postmark date, and your closing office will normally order a tax certificate.

Dallas County Tax Office deadlines
EventDate or rule
Statements mailedOctober, after rates are set
Delinquent afterJanuary 31
Appraisal protest deadlineNo later than May 15
Mail paymentsPostmark date is used
Sent to attorney, business personal propertyApril 1
Sent to attorney, all other propertyJuly 1

The Dallas County Tax Office posts the same schedule online.

Whatever is owed in back taxes, penalty and interest comes out of your share at the closing table, so ask for payoff figures early. Come February 1 the collector tacks on a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest, and that penalty grows to 12 percent by July 1.

Some owners can request a payment plan, and a penalty waiver request generally has to be written. Already behind? The Dallas County Tax Office customer care line, 214-653-7811, can review your accounts before any contract is signed.

sections.h2: What if I missed a tax bill?
sections.html: Phone the Dallas County Tax Office ahead of the cutoff that sends an account to a collection attorney. The handoff to attorneys is April 1 for business personal property and July 1 for everything else. Plans on delinquent homestead taxes are sometimes available, and in narrow situations you can put a request in writing asking the collector to waive penalty and interest. Ask what the office offers, then tell the closing office the answer so the settlement figures come out right.

sections.h2: Homestead rules and a Lancaster sale
sections.html:
The exemption stays with the owner who earned it. Whoever buys your house files a fresh application under their own name. Every school district has to exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value. An owner past 65, or one with a disability, receives $60,000 beyond that along with a school tax ceiling.

  • Applications are generally due by April 30.
  • Inherited house with no heir on the recorded deed? Bring an affidavit of ownership, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to the appraisal district.
  • A disabled veteran may qualify for a partial or total exemption based on a disability rating.

The Comptroller explains the rules on its exemptions page.

sections.h2: Repairs, permits and what they cost
sections.html: Prices swing from house to house, so collect two written bids before choosing whether to fix anything. Check with the City of Lancaster about permit rules before starting major work, and hold onto any permits so the buyer's inspector can see them. If the work list is long, a cash offer lets you hand the repairs to someone else, usually at a lower price.

Housing here is mostly single-family, but multi-family property makes up about a quarter of it. If you sell with tenants in place, go through each lease for its term, deposit and notice language, then send a written summary along to the buyer or the closing office.

Tenant behind on rent, or a lease you want to wrap up before showings? The Dallas County court clerk or a Texas attorney can tell you which notice fits. An investor will often take an occupied house as it stands, which can save you a vacant stretch with no rent coming in.

The Dallas County Clerk records general warranty, special warranty and quitclaim deeds, along with other instruments. Before recording, either a notary or other authorized officer must acknowledge the conveyance or two subscribing witnesses must swear to it.

The clerk charges $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after. The closing office usually files the deed after funding.

One folder should hold your deed, a survey if you have one, this year's Dallas County tax statement, each lender's payoff letter and any HOA or deed restriction papers. If the house carries a homestead exemption, jot down who qualified and when.

Add receipts for roof, HVAC, plumbing and foundation jobs, plus permits where the city asked for them. Inspectors and buyers request these first, and a complete folder lets you reply within a day.

  • Photo ID and proof of ownership for the closing office.
  • Lease copies and tenant contact details if the house is rented.
  • Utility account details so service can switch over at closing.

The choice usually comes down to condition and calendar. Putting the house on the market reaches the most shoppers, yet the repairs, the showing schedule and the buyer's loan approval are all places where a Lancaster deal can slip. A cash purchase gives up some price in return for certainty, with fewer showings, no lender to wait on and a closing date you have a say in.

Lancaster's mix of single-family and multi-family housing means investors are active, and some will take a house with deferred maintenance or sitting tenants. Collect two or three written offers and subtract loan payoffs, back taxes and recording costs from each one, since the top number is rarely the one you keep.

sections.h2: Questions to ask the tax office
sections.html:
A short call can prevent a late surprise at the closing table. Ask what is owed today and what the figure will be on your expected closing date. Ask whether a payment plan or a penalty waiver request is open on the account. Ask which exemptions are on file and who qualified for them. If the account is close to the April 1 or July 1 attorney cutoff, say so and ask how that would change the payoff.

Write down the answers and send them to your closing office. The same facts will be requested again later, so keeping them on hand cuts down the phone tag.

1. Call the tax office for current balances and ask whether a plan is open.
  2. Collect offers, compare what each would leave after payoffs, and choose one.
  3. The closing office orders the tax certificate and the loan payoff figures.
  4. You sign the deed before a notary, and funds are released at closing.
  5. The deed goes to the county clerk for recording.

A buyer paying cash skips the lender's appraisal, so the calendar is mostly set by how fast title work finishes.

faqs.q: When are Lancaster property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: Unpaid balances turn delinquent after January 31. Dallas County says state law then requires penalty and interest.

faqs.q: What is the protest deadline for a Lancaster appraisal?
faqs.a: No later than May 15. The Dallas Central Appraisal District can walk you through the process.

faqs.q: Who sends the Lancaster tax statement?
faqs.a: The Dallas County Tax Office. Statements are mailed in October to the address on the account.

faqs.q: Does a Lancaster deed need a notary?
faqs.a: Yes. A notary or similar officer must take the acknowledgment, or two subscribing witnesses must swear to it, before the county clerk will record the deed.

faqs.q: Can heirs claim a homestead on an inherited Lancaster house?
faqs.a: They may. Someone inheriting the house who is not named on the recorded deed can still file for the exemption by supplying an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.
